ns2:section.sectionText: VERY DEGENERATE ATOMIC GASES. With the aid of laser cooling and other techniques it has become possible in the last few years not only to stabilize dilute gases of alkali atoms (and some others) but to cool them into the temperature range where the effects of quantum degeneracy become dominant; in particular, both Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) and Fermi degeneracy have been realized in these systems. PHYS 498VDG will cover trapping, cooling and diagnostic techniques, the general theory of BEC and the principal physical properties of trapped BEC gases, special effects associated with the presence of multiple hyperfine species, Bose gases in optical lattices and questions concerning the possible onset of Cooper pairing in degenerate Fermi alkali gases. Other topics may be included on request. Prerequisites: basic graduate quantum mechanics, basic graduate statistical mechanics and an undergraduate course in atomic physics.
